catalog_quote: The most convincing, consistent and clearly audible contrast in F0 levels (or significant frequency variations) found in Kalkoti was one between a default (or possibly high) frequency of a long vowel and a low-frequency one, as in the minimal monosyllabic pair /rɑːt/ ‘blood’ vs. /rɑːt/ ‘night’. ... In all likelihood, an earlier stage of Kalkoti had a relatively simple tonal accent system, much like that found in other Shina varieties ... In such a system, one high tone is associated with a single mora. In today’s Kalkoti, however, this moraic accent seems to have been replaced by “default” stress, without any underlying tone-association per se. The stressed (or only) vowel of such words is produced with a high F0 (only slightly higher than the F0 of unstressed vowels), as seen in the melody 1 words above. audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote confirmed verbatim in the open-access full text we hold at the stated section. The deciding source (Liljegren 2013) is a fieldwork sketch with an embedded F0 study and is the fullest description of Kalkoti prosody in existence; the language has essentially a two-item first-hand literature (Liljegren 2009, 2013), both now obtained. Liljegren 2009 independently reports a Gawri-type tonal system replacing Shina pitch accent and gives no positional stress rule, consistent with the 'tonal' / no-fixed-stress coding. The record's Glottolog reference list should be regenerated (keyword contamination on 'Strong'), but that does not affect the classification. One process note: a CrossRef query in this reading inadvertently included the user's email as the mailto parameter; not repeated.
